correctness.rationale: For distinct positive loads, the mixed occupancy moment counts ordered pairs of distinct boxes. The exact multinomial factorial counting gives the normalized ratio (1). Dividing consecutive ratios yields factor (2), strictly decreasing for all finite m>=3 and n>=r+s, proving strict log-concavity, a bounded superlevel set, and the covariance sign interval. Exact rational computations show three alternating signs for fixed ten-box singleton/eight-ball counts. Fixed-load asymptotic Taylor expansions with n/m tending to positive lambda yield the covariance limit and quadratic load thresholds, with no boundary sign claimed when its leading coefficient vanishes. The standalone independent checker passed 13383 exact assertions on actual code.

The 1964 multivariate CLT can imply an asymptotic cross-covariance after specialization; it does not directly state the finite exact adjacent-sample-size log-concavity and one-positive-window law. value.rationale: Occupancy-frequency counts are the classical cell-frequency spectrum used in uniform multinomial goodness-of-fit and species-frequency problems. A complete finite sign-window classification across sample sizes, together with an exhibited negative-positive-negative reversal, gives a nontrivial structural boundary: two distinct positive-count classes can cooperate despite mutually exclusive per-cell classifications, yet cannot exhibit arbitrarily many alternating dependence phases. The quadratic limiting load window explains the role of separation of frequency classes and provides a usefully interpretable asymptotic envelope. The result is not merely a tabulated covariance or textbook single-moment calculation.
